patch.value: pm package manage --fix-managed-state holds the extension state lock across every remote update lookup, so a raised update-check budget lengthens how long concurrent package actions wait

Raised by CodeRabbit on PR 1752 (outside-diff comment on src/sdk/extension.ts, the prepareExploreManageState path). With --fix-managed-state, dispatchExtensionAction wraps the whole manage handler in withExtensionInstallLock. That handler adopts unmanaged packages and then calls refreshManagedExtensionUpdates, so the lock stays held while every npm view and git ls-remote runs, four at a time. The refresh never persists its result, so it does not need the lock. Behaviour is unchanged at the default 10-second budget, but PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS (pm-5kfzjh) can raise each lookup to 120 seconds. A concurrent install, uninstall or adopt then waits longer for the lock and can fail with a lock conflict. Proposed: keep only the adoption read and write under the lock, and run the refresh and runtime probe after it is released.

manage --fix-managed-state holds the extension state lock only for the adoption read and write; the remote update refresh and runtime probe run after the lock is released, with the same results and offline behaviour; a test proves a concurrent locked package action is not blocked by a slow lookup; manage without --fix-managed-state is unchanged
A slow or long-budget update lookup never holds the extension state lock
With --fix-managed-state the lock spans every remote update lookup, up to the configured budget per lookup
